newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin sees economy EU ready after 2002.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin sees economy EU ready after 2002.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Thursday the country's economy will be ready for entry to European Union (EU) between years 2002 and 2005.

In a speech at the Bratislava Economics University, Kozlik also said a real GDP will have to grow by at least five percent a year by the time of entry to EU if the country wants to succeed on the EU market.
"From a realistic point of view, we see the economy ready for entry to EU between years 2002 and 2005...then we may be prepared to succeed in the EU competition," Kozlik said.
He added that privatisation of Slovakia's strategic companies will have to be carried out during the next government's term, between years 1998 and 2002.
"That time, between 1998 and 2002, will be the key period for privatisation of strategic companies, and they definitely have to be privatised," Kozlik said.
In 1995 the government listed dozens of state enterprises as strategic, effectively excluding them from privatisation process or at least leaving some under state control.
The list included the monopoly gas distributor SPP, the Slovak Telecommunications company and Transpetrol, which operates oil pipelines for Russian supplies to the West.
Kozlik would not elaborate on how the privatisation should be carried out, nor did he say whether the government was already working on the sell-offs.
Kozlik said the government was preparing a package of unspecified measures to help improve the structure of GDP.
Slovak GDP rose 6.9 percent year-on-year in 1996, compared with a 6.8 percent increase in 1995. However, a large portion of the growth was caused by high domestic demand.
"We know about the problem of the structure of GDP, and I can say we are preparing some measures to improve it," he said.
"The government hopes to succeed in changing the structure by the end of the year," Kozlik added. He did not elaborate.
Kozlik said the economy continued to grow in the first two months of this year, referring mainly to a 2.2 percent year- on-year increase of industrial output in February.
He also said exports showed the first signs of revival at the beginning of this year, boosted mainly by an increase in production in the engineering sector.
